title: Mirzapur: The Movie Crosses Rs 315 Crore Worldwide on Day 18
excerpt: The Gurmeet Singh-directed crime saga, starring Pankaj Tripathi and Ali Fazal, has become the third Hindi film of 2026 to cross Rs 300 crore at the global box office.
body:
• Mirzapur: The Movie earned an estimated Rs 1.8 crore net on day 18, its third Monday, taking its India net total to roughly Rs 217.5 crore, according to Sacnilk-based trade estimates.
  • Worldwide gross now stands near Rs 315 crore, making it the third Hindi film of 2026 to cross the Rs 300-crore mark globally.
  • The Gurmeet Singh-directed crime saga, based on the hit Prime Video series, released on September 4 and stars Pankaj Tripathi, Ali Fazal, Divyenndu and Ravi Kishan.
  • Trade trackers project a lifetime finish approaching Rs 350 crore worldwide, which would place it among the year's biggest Indian grossers.

Third Monday holds the line

The third Monday is where most theatrical runs go to fade. Mirzapur: The Movie refused. The film collected an estimated Rs 1.75-1.90 crore net on day 18, a drop of roughly 60 percent from its third Sunday but enough to carry its India net total to about Rs 217.5 crore, according to Sacnilk-based estimates carried by trade trackers. Koimoi's own day-wise tracker puts the 18-day India net slightly higher at Rs 221.67 crore, with a worldwide gross of Rs 314.09 crore.

The third week has followed the classic weekday-slowdown curve: about Rs 2.7 crore on the third Friday, Rs 4.5 crore on Saturday and close to Rs 5 crore on Sunday, before Monday's dip. Khel Ja, citing Sacnilk, reported the film played across 4,456 shows on day 18 at 14 percent occupancy, with overseas markets adding another Rs 50 lakh gross on the day to take the overseas total to Rs 56.25 crore.

From streaming phenomenon to box-office force

Mirzapur began as a Prime Video series that built one of the most recognizable crime universes in Hindi streaming. The film version, presented by Amazon MGM Studios and produced by Ritesh Sidhwani and Farhan Akhtar under Excel Entertainment, converted that small-screen equity into a theatrical event. It marks the feature directorial debut of Gurmeet Singh, with a screenplay by series writer Puneet Krishna.

The ensemble brings back the franchise's core faces: Pankaj Tripathi as Kaleen Bhaiya, Ali Fazal as Guddu Pandit, Divyenndu as Munna Tripathi and Ravi Kishan in a central antagonistic turn, alongside Jitendra Kumar, Harshita Gaur, Rasika Dugal, Abhishek Banerjee, Rajesh Tailang and Kulbhushan Kharbanda. The film opened on September 4 to about Rs 28 crore net on day one, powered by exceptional turnout in mass centres across Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, and crossed Rs 100 crore worldwide in its opening weekend alone.

The Rs 300-crore club and the road ahead

Crossing Rs 300 crore worldwide made Mirzapur: The Movie only the third Hindi film of 2026 to reach the milestone. It has already overtaken recent notable releases including the animated Mahavatar Narsimha (Rs 301 crore) and the Malayalam actioner Lokah Chapter One: Chandra (Rs 304 crore), and sits ninth on the list of the year's highest-grossing Indian films, according to Hungama Express.

The next landmark is Rs 350 crore. If the current hold continues, trade watchers expect the film to get there before its run ends, which would put it ahead of titles like Jana Nayagan, Toxic and Peddi. Competition remains real: Hanuman Ansh, released August 7, is still in theatres and has crossed Rs 350 crore worldwide itself. But Mirzapur's weekday resilience suggests the franchise's core audience is far from done.

Why the diaspora showed up

Overseas, the film has earned over $5 million, with North America and the Middle East doing the heavy lifting, according to Hungama Express. That is the streaming dividend at work: years of Mirzapur on Prime Video gave diaspora audiences a familiarity with these characters that most original theatrical properties cannot buy. For Indian viewers abroad, the film played less like a gamble and more like a reunion, and the box office reflects it.
